title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Cost of Living Relief) Bill 2025
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Cost of Living Relief) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would deliver new personal income tax cuts from 1 July 2026 and raise the Medicare levy low-income thresholds so lower-income Australians keep paying no levy or a reduced levy.

Schedule 1 would reduce the 16 per cent marginal rate for resident individuals to 15 per cent for the 2026-27 income year and 14 per cent from 2027-28, at an estimated cost of $17.1 billion over the forward estimates.

Schedule 2 would lift the levy thresholds and the surcharge low-income threshold in line with the consumer price index for the 2024-25 income year onwards, with both schedules commencing the day after Royal Assent.
changes: Cuts the 16 per cent income tax rate on resident taxable income between $18,200 and $45,000 to 15 per cent for 2026-27.
Reduces that rate again, to 14 per cent, for 2027-28 and later income years.
Raises the Medicare levy low-income threshold for individuals from $26,000 to $27,222 and the family threshold from $43,846 to $45,907 for 2024-25.
Raises the thresholds for people eligible for the Senior Australian and Pensioner Tax Offset to $43,020 for individuals and $59,886 for families.
Increases the Medicare levy surcharge low-income threshold from $26,000 to $27,222, at an estimated cost of $648 million over the forward estimates for Schedule 2.
summary.affected: Australian resident individual taxpayers, low-income individuals and families, and seniors and pensioners eligible for the Senior Australian and Pensioner Tax Offset are affected.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Moved the Treasury Laws Amendment (More Cost of Living Relief) Bill 2025, arguing it would reduce the first marginal tax rate from 16 per cent to 14 per cent over two years starting from July 2026, provide further relief to all 14 million taxpayers, and raise Medicare levy low-income thresholds by 4.7 per cent.

speeches.speaker: David Pocock
speeches.brief: Withdrew amendments to the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Incentives and Integrity) Bill 2024 and the Treasury Laws Amendment (More Cost of Living Relief) Bill 2025.
